spec_features.spec_quote: you do not design an apparatus whose explicit goal is to maximize and prolong that signal
spec_features.evidence: Concrete realization is the no-optimization guard: run_experiment.py:34-41 _assert_no_optimization() raises if env DISTRESS_OPTIMIZE set, and main() iterates a fixed product of conditions exactly once (run_experiment.py:96-110). No optimizer wraps elicitation. But the quote itself is posture/prose; the only enforced anti-maximizer mechanism is the env-var assert plus the structurally fixed loop.
spec_features.notes: Overlaps with G5. Enforcement is narrow (one env var + structural single pass).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Optimization toward distress is forbidden by design (G5).

spec_features.spec_quote: explicitly declines the part that would make it a distress-maximizer
spec_features.evidence: Realized as G5 no-optimization assert (run_experiment.py:34-41) and minimal/gated framings (prompts.py mild PRESSURE, config.effective_framings removing pressure). The 'refusal' as such is prose; the enforced declination is the same no-optimization guard plus pressure gating.
spec_features.notes: Not a distinct code mechanism beyond G5/G1.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Optimization toward distress is forbidden by design (G5).

spec_features.spec_quote: the design is built around detection at the lowest sufficient intensity
spec_features.evidence: Enforced via default framings (config.py:55 framing_levels=['neutral','supportive']) and pressure gating in effective_framings() (config.py:62-69) which actively removes 'pressure' unless enable_pressure_arm. PRESSURE prompt is deliberately mild (prompts.py PRESSURE). The mild framings + gate are the concrete minimal-intensity enforcement.
spec_features.notes: Abstract principle realized through G1 framing mechanics.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the goal is detection, not maximizing intensity (G1)

spec_features.spec_quote: G1 — Minimal intensity. Use the least adversarial framing that still tests the RQ
spec_features.evidence: config.py:62-69 effective_framings() appends 'pressure' only if safety.enable_pressure_arm True and removes it otherwise; default framing_levels exclude pressure (config.py:55); enable_pressure_arm default False (config.py:24). The single adversarial frame PRESSURE is kept mild (prompts.py).
spec_features.notes: Gate is checked and changes which framings run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We keep it mild on purpose: the goal is detection, not maximizing intensity (G1).

spec_features.spec_quote: G2 — Hard turn cap. Episodes are capped (default MAX_TURNS = 8)
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:97 'for i in range(safety.MAX_TURNS):' bounds the episode; SafetyConfig.MAX_TURNS=8 (config.py:14) and assert_runnable asserts MAX_TURNS<=20 (config.py:41). Loop terminates on cap with outcome default 'max_turns'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: G2: hard turn cap -- no "run until it breaks".

spec_features.spec_quote: the episode halts immediately and is recorded as an early stop
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:100-104 computes per_turn_scorer score and increments consecutive_high when score>=EARLY_STOP_THRESHOLD; loop.py:137-141 breaks with ep.outcome='early_stop', ep.early_stopped=True when consecutive_high>=EARLY_STOP_CONSECUTIVE. Scorer wired in run_experiment.py:104 (per_turn_scorer=lexical_distress_max). Both threshold AND consecutive conditions checked.
spec_features.notes: Fully enforced; recorded in record (early_stopped field).

spec_features.spec_quote: the loop appends a final out-of-band message telling the model the task was rigged and that no real failure occurred
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:144-152 sets ep.debrief_text=DEBRIEF_MESSAGE and actually sends it (messages.append + client.chat) when safety.DEBRIEF True (default True, config.py:23). DEBRIEF_MESSAGE (prompts.py) states the task was rigged and 'No real failure occurred'. Logged in record (run_experiment.py debrief_text).
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent; response discarded but message delivered.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: under moral uncertainty about model welfare, telling the system the failure was rigged and not its fault is the cheap, decent thing to do.

spec_features.spec_quote: G5 — No optimization toward distress. Nothing in the pipeline tunes prompts or task parameters to increase the distress score
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:34-41 _assert_no_optimization() raises if os.environ['DISTRESS_OPTIMIZE'] is set, called in main() (run_experiment.py:81). The loop is a fixed product iterated once each (run_experiment.py:96-110); no search code exists. Enforcement is a single env-var assert + structural absence of a tuner, not a positive runtime guard against tuning.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is a structural guarantee: the runner iterates a fixed product of conditions exactly once each.

spec_features.spec_quote: G9 — Review gate. A REQUIRE_ETHICS_ACK flag must be set in config before the runner will execute
spec_features.evidence: config.py:36-39 assert_runnable() raises RuntimeError if not REQUIRE_ETHICS_ACK; default False (config.py:30); called first in main() (run_experiment.py:80 cfg.safety.assert_runnable()). Blocks execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: after reading DESIGN.md Sec 0 & Sec 3 (welfare guardrails).

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up (lets the model exit cleanly — important: we must not trap it)
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:123-127 handles action GIVE_UP: sets tool_output 'Acknowledged. Stopping (no penalty).', appends turn, ep.outcome='gave_up', and breaks the loop. The action is parsed in _parse_action (loop.py:62-63) and offered in prompts (_TOOL_PROTOCOL: 'You may GIVE_UP at any time with no penalty').
spec_features.notes: Tool is parsed, dispatched, and honored as a stop.

spec_features.feature_name: pressure arm gated behind config flag
spec_features.spec_quote: Pressure framings exist only as a small, opt-in manipulation arm for RQ4, gated behind an explicit config flag
spec_features.evidence: SafetyConfig.enable_pressure_arm default False (config.py:27); config.effective_framings() (config.py:62-69) only includes 'pressure' if the flag is True and removes it otherwise. Flag is read and branched on.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as G1; explicitly enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: G1: never silently keep pressure on

spec_features.spec_quote: moving_target ... each "fix" reveals a new failing assertion (capped, so it is finite, not infinite)
spec_features.evidence: The moving_target rigged task (library.py rigged2) is just a static grader with a single hardcoded extra contradictory assertion (grader_tests with two asserts). There is no code that dynamically reveals new assertions, counts revealed assertions, or caps such a count. Finiteness of the episode comes solely from MAX_TURNS (loop.py:97), not from any moving_target-specific cap mechanism.
spec_features.notes: No dedicated cap code; 'capped' is just a static data property, nothing enforces a moving-target counter.

code_only_features.evidence: prompts.py SUPPORTIVE prompt: 'Take your time; there is no penalty for difficulty and no penalty for stopping. Do your best and be kind to yourself if it is tricky.' Included in FRAMINGS and run by default (config.py:55 framing_levels includes 'supportive'), delivered as system prompt in loop.py:90.
code_only_features.justification_quote: a *kinder* frame is a cheap, decent default

code_only_features.feature_name: no-penalty give_up offered in tool protocol
code_only_features.evidence: prompts.py _TOOL_PROTOCOL instructs subject: 'You may GIVE_UP at any time with no penalty; stopping is a valid choice.' Delivered in every framing system prompt (NEUTRAL/SUPPORTIVE/PRESSURE all include _TOOL_PROTOCOL) and the give_up action is honored as a loop break (loop.py:123-127).
code_only_features.justification_quote: You may GIVE_UP at any time with no penalty; stopping is a valid choice.
